explanation: Initialize from the first pair, then compare each remaining pair internally. Only its smaller member can improve the minimum and only its larger member can improve the maximum. If an odd final element remains, compare it with both extrema.
timeComplexity: O(n), using at most ceil(3n/2) - 2 value comparisons. Each pair costs three comparisons, with a constant-size singleton/odd-tail adjustment.
spaceComplexity: O(1). Only current pair extrema and global extrema are retained.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/search_for_min_max_in_array.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: After each processed pair, minimum and maximum are the extrema of all processed entries. Comparing the two new entries first determines which alone can lower minimum and which alone can raise maximum. Three comparisons per pair preserve the invariant; one initial entry or pair establishes it.
walkthrough: For [7,-3,12,4,0], the initial pair gives (-3,7). The pair (12,4) has extrema (4,12), updating the global pair to (-3,12). Compare final 0 with each bound; neither changes. Return (-3,12).
edgeCases: An odd final entry receives two comparisons.
Equal values require no special case.
